newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay buys Dexter's 50% in D&S Plastics.
newsitem.headline: Solvay buys Dexter's 50% in D&S Plastics.

text.p: Belgian chemicals group Solvay SA said on Tuesday it bought the 50 percent in D&S Plastics International owned by Dexter Corp of the U.S.
The purchase is through Solvay's Solvay America Inc, which already owns the other half of D&S Plastics.
D&S Plastics with plants in Texas and headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, is the largest supplier of egineered polyolefin materials, mainly for car bumpers, to the North American car industry.
Solvay aims to turn D&S Plastics into a global supplier of car materials, which the group sees as a core business.
Solvay said in a statement it was determined to strengthen its automotive business further.
Solvay gave no details of the purchasing agreement, which was signed earlier on Tuesday.
D&S Plastics has a staff of 300 and sales of some $100 million.

A Solvay spokesman said sales growth was on the cards. D&S Plastics has market share of 50 percent in the Nafta countries -- the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The Belgian group employs more than 35,000 people. It had 1996 turnover of $8.8 billion.
Wall Street-listed Dexter Corp supplies specialty materials to the aerospace, electronics, food packaging and medical markets. It had 1996 sales of $1.1 billion.
